# Is the Digital SAT Harder? 2026 Guide to What Changed


## TL;DR


The Digital SAT is not officially harder than the paper SAT, but it can feel harder because the test is adaptive. Each section has two modules, and strong performance in Module 1 can route you to a higher-difficulty Module 2. The Digital SAT is also shorter, gives students more time per question, uses shorter reading passages, and provides a built-in Desmos calculator.


The biggest difficulty change is strategic: **Module 1 accuracy matters because it influences which second module you receive.** College Board's scoring system also considers question difficulty and other item characteristics, so the number of questions you get right does not translate into a fixed number of points.


There is evidence that newer Digital SAT practice materials are more challenging than some of the earliest practice tests, but that should not be presented as proof that the actual SAT gets harder every year. For students preparing in 2026, the safest approach is to practice with the most current official Bluebook tests and train specifically for the higher-difficulty second module.


If you’re just starting to prepare, a[diagnostic and study plan](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/digital-sat-prep) built for the adaptive format will save you from the surprises that catch most students off guard.


> **Quick Answer: Is the Digital SAT Harder?**
>
>
> The Digital SAT is not officially designed to be harder than the paper SAT. College Board’s concordance studies found that digital and paper SAT scores measure the same underlying skills and can be used comparably. However, the Digital SAT can feel harder because it is adaptive, sends stronger-performing students to a more difficult second module, uses screen-based reading, and gives each question greater importance within a shorter test. At the same time, students get more time per question, shorter reading passages, and a built-in Desmos calculator.
>
>
> **Bottom line:** The Digital SAT is not inherently harder, but its adaptive format changes where the difficulty appears. For high scorers, the biggest challenge is usually the harder second module, especially in Math.


## Digital SAT Difficulty at a Glance


Question


Short Answer


Is the Digital SAT harder than the paper SAT?


Not by design. College Board says equivalent scores represent comparable achievement.


Is the Digital SAT easier in some ways?


Yes. It is shorter, gives more time per question, uses shorter reading passages, and includes Desmos.


Is it harder in some ways?


Yes. The adaptive format can create a significant difficulty jump in Module 2, particularly for high-scoring students.


Does doing well in Module 1 make the test harder?


Usually, yes. Strong Module 1 performance can route you to the higher-difficulty second module.


Is Math Module 2 the hardest part?


For many high-scoring students, it is the most challenging portion because it contains a higher concentration of difficult questions.


Is the Digital SAT objectively getting harder every year?


There is evidence that newer practice materials have become more challenging, but there is not enough public College Board evidence to state that the actual SAT is systematically getting harder every year.


## What Is the Digital SAT?


The digital SAT is the fully computer-based version of the SAT, launched in the United States in March 2024. Students take it on a laptop or tablet through College Board’s Bluebook app. It replaced the paper SAT entirely.


Here are the basics:


-


**Total time:** 2 hours and 14 minutes (down from roughly 3 hours)


-


**Total questions:** 98 (down from 154)


-


**Sections:** Reading & Writing (54 questions) and Math (44 questions)


-


**Format:** Adaptive, meaning the test adjusts difficulty based on your performance


-


**Calculator:** Built-in Desmos graphing calculator available on every math question


The College Board’s vice president of College Readiness Assessments, Priscilla Rodriguez, described it as “easier to take, easier to give, and more relevant.” That framing is accurate for the logistics. Whether it’s easier to score well on is another matter entirely.


For a full breakdown of the test structure, see this[guide to the digital SAT format](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/digital-sat-format-sections-modules-scoring) .


---


## How Adaptive Testing Works (And Why It Matters for Difficulty)


Adaptive testing is the single most important concept for understanding whether the digital SAT is harder. Here’s how it works.


Each section (Reading & Writing and Math) is split into two modules. Module 1 contains a broad mix of easy, medium, and hard questions. Your performance on Module 1 determines which version of Module 2 you receive: a harder one or an easier one.


This is module-level adaptation, not question-level. The questions within each module are pre-set, so you can skip around and return to questions freely within a module. But you cannot go back to Module 1 once you’ve moved to Module 2.


Why does this matter so much? Because the module you’re routed to determines your score ceiling.


### How Module 2 Affects Your Score Range


Second Module


What It Means


Score Implication


Higher-difficulty Module 2


You performed strongly enough in Module 1 to receive the more difficult question mix.


Opens access to the full range of section scores, including the top of the 800-point scale.


Lower-difficulty Module 2


Your Module 1 performance resulted in a lower-difficulty question mix.


A range of scores is still possible, but reaching the very highest section scores is generally associated with the higher-difficulty route.


**Important:** Do not think of the Digital SAT as having a simple “hard module = 800” and “easy module = 630 maximum” scoring rule. College Board uses Item Response Theory (IRT), which considers the difficulty and other characteristics of the questions you answer. College Board states that a range of section scores is possible regardless of which second module you receive.


If you end up in the easier Module 2, you could answer every single remaining question correctly and still never break 630 in that section. That’s roughly a 1260 composite ceiling. For students aiming at competitive colleges, being routed to the easy module is essentially game over for that test date.


This creates a dynamic the paper SAT never had. The test literally becomes harder for students who are doing well, and that’s by design. Getting the harder Module 2 is a reward, not a punishment, because those harder questions carry more scoring weight.


---


## Equating vs. Curving: How Scoring Actually Works


Many students worry that a harder test date means lower scores. This misunderstanding comes from confusing curving with equating.


The digital SAT does not use a curve. Your score never depends on how other test-takers performed. Instead, College Board uses a statistical process called **equating** , which adjusts the raw-to-scaled score conversion based on the difficulty of the specific test form you received.


If your test form was harder, you can miss more questions and still earn the same scaled score as someone who took an easier form and missed fewer. Before launching the digital SAT, College Board ran two large concordance studies and published a straight-line concordance: a 1200 on the digital SAT represents the same level of achievement as a 1200 on the paper SAT.


### How Digital SAT Scoring Actually Works


The Digital SAT does not use a simple one-point-per-question scoring system. College Board uses Item Response Theory (IRT) to calculate section scores.


That means your final score can depend on:


-


Which questions you answered correctly or incorrectly


-


The difficulty and characteristics of those questions


-


Your overall pattern of responses


-


The adaptive module you received


As a result, two students can answer the same number of questions correctly and receive different section scores.


There is also no guessing penalty. If you do not know an answer, you should still select an answer before time expires.


### Equating Is Not the Same as a Curve


The SAT is not graded on a traditional curve. Your score does not rise or fall because other students performed better or worse.


Instead, College Board uses equating to account for differences in difficulty between test forms. The goal is for the same scaled score to represent a comparable level of achievement across different SAT administrations. College Board's concordance studies also found that digital SAT scores can be compared directly with scores from the previous paper-and-pencil SAT.


For a deeper look at how this scoring system works, read this[explanation of adaptive scoring](https://miyagilabs.ai/blog/how-is-the-digital-sat-scored-adaptive-scoring) .

## What’s Easier About the Digital SAT


Compared to the paper version, several changes genuinely make the digital SAT less difficult or less stressful.


**More time per question.** The digital SAT offers approximately 43% more time per question than the paper version. Math questions get roughly 95 seconds each (up from 75-86 seconds), and Reading & Writing questions get about 71 seconds each. That extra breathing room is real.


**Shorter test overall.** At 2 hours and 14 minutes versus 3 hours, fatigue is a much smaller factor. Eighty percent of students who took the pilot digital version said they found it less stressful, and 84% of students along with 99% of testing staff reported a better overall experience.


**Shorter reading passages.** Gone are the 750-word essays with 10+ attached questions. Each Reading & Writing question now comes with its own short passage of roughly 100 words. If you struggled with long-passage stamina on the old SAT, this is a major relief.


**Built-in Desmos calculator on all math.** The paper SAT restricted calculators to one section. The digital SAT gives you[Desmos on every math question](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/desmos) , which provides a clear speed advantage for finding intersections, plugging in answer choices, visualizing quadratics, and solving systems of equations.


**Built-in tools.** Highlighter, annotation, question flagging, and an on-screen timer are all baked into the Bluebook interface.


---


## What’s Harder About the Digital SAT


The “easier” side gets a lot of attention. The harder side often catches students by surprise.


**Fewer questions means less room for error.** With only 98 questions instead of 154, each question carries more weight. On the paper SAT, you could absorb a few mistakes across 154 questions without major damage. On the digital version, every wrong answer stings more.


**The Module 2 difficulty jump can be brutal.** Students who perform well on Module 1 get routed to a significantly harder Module 2. Practitioners on Reddit report that this difficulty jump far exceeds what Bluebook practice tests prepare them for. Students on r/SAT have described encountering questions that diverged significantly from the familiar patterns found in College Board’s practice materials and Khan Academy resources.


**Screen-based reading may reduce comprehension.** Research has consistently shown that readers demonstrate better comprehension when reading on paper versus screens. One student journalist at Arcadia Quill cited this research in arguing the digital SAT is genuinely harder. You also can’t physically mark up passages the way you could on paper, scribbling notes in the margins or underlining key phrases with a pencil. The digital highlighter tool helps, but it’s not the same.


**The scoring curve feels harsher.** Because wrong answers in Module 2 carry different weight than in Module 1, and because the adaptive routing creates distinct score ceilings, many students feel the grading system is less forgiving than the paper version.


**Desmos dependency is now a trap.** This deserves its own section.

The important distinction is that these features can make the **experience** harder without proving that the Digital SAT measures students more harshly overall. College Board's research was specifically designed to maintain comparability between digital and paper SAT scores.


## Why Does the Digital SAT Feel Harder Than the Paper SAT?


The Digital SAT can feel harder even when its overall difficulty is designed to remain comparable with the previous SAT. The biggest reason is that the difficulty is distributed differently.


### 1. Strong performance can lead to harder questions


The Digital SAT is multistage adaptive. Your performance in Module 1 influences the difficulty mix of Module 2. Students who perform strongly can therefore encounter a noticeably more difficult second module.


### 2. The test gives you less room to lose focus


There are 98 questions rather than the 154 questions on the previous SAT. Because the test uses fewer questions to measure the same skills, each question becomes part of a more sophisticated scoring model.


### 3. Screen reading is a different skill


The Digital SAT presents short passages or passage pairs followed by individual questions. Students who are more comfortable reading and annotating on paper may need time to adjust to the digital interface.


### 4. Hard questions can require more than calculator fluency


Desmos can make many Digital SAT Math problems faster, but it does not replace algebraic reasoning, mathematical modeling, or conceptual understanding. The most difficult problems may require students to recognize the underlying relationship before choosing the best method.


### 5. The adaptive format creates psychological pressure


Students know that Module 1 affects what they see next. That can make an otherwise manageable question feel more consequential than it would on a linear test.


**The result:** The Digital SAT may not be objectively harder overall, but the experience can feel more demanding because the test concentrates difficulty differently.


## Desmos: The Double-Edged Sword


When the digital SAT launched, Desmos felt like a cheat code. Students could graph their way through math problems without fully understanding the underlying concepts.


College Board noticed. Tutors from SupertutorTV have pointed out that hard Module 2 math questions now use variables instead of numbers specifically to block Desmos-only solving strategies. As one tutor put it: “You have to know how to do it without Desmos, too, because in Math Module 2, they use variables instead of numbers specifically to block that strategy.”


Three themes keep repeating among prep professionals: the adaptive Math Module 2 is genuinely difficult, Desmos alone won’t carry you through it, and College Board has tightened questions to ensure that’s the case.


Desmos remains a powerful tool. It just can’t be your only tool. Students should learn both when to use it and when to put it aside. For guided practice on this balance, try these[Desmos practice problems](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/desmos/practice) that mirror the tricky question types College Board now favors.

## Is the Digital SAT Getting Harder Over Time?


There is evidence that the Digital SAT preparation landscape has become more challenging since the test launched, but it is too strong to say that College Board has definitively made the live SAT harder every year.


One of the clearest pieces of evidence comes from the official practice-test ecosystem. In February 2025, College Board released new Digital SAT practice tests and removed some earlier tests. An independent analysis by Piqosity found that the newer practice tests appeared somewhat more difficult than some of the earliest Digital SAT practice materials, particularly in the harder second modules.


However, this distinction matters:


**Harder practice materials do not automatically prove that the real SAT has become harder.**


College Board continues to use equating and IRT-based scoring to maintain comparable score meaning across different test forms. Its current documentation states that the SAT measures the same underlying knowledge and skills and that scores remain comparable across forms.


### What Changed for Students?


The safest conclusion is that students should no longer rely heavily on the earliest Digital SAT practice materials when judging their readiness.


For 2026 preparation, prioritize:


1.


Current official Bluebook full-length practice tests


2.


Official SAT question-bank problems


3.


Hard-difficulty questions in your weakest domains


4.


Timed practice on an actual computer or tablet


5.


Practice that prepares you for both possible Module 2 difficulty levels


College Board currently provides official full-length digital practice tests through Bluebook, and says its practice tests are designed to be representative of the actual SAT.


**Bottom line:** The evidence supports saying that some newer Digital SAT practice materials are harder than early materials. It does not justify claiming that the actual SAT gets objectively harder every year.

## Module 2: The Heart of the Difficulty Question


If there’s one place where the “is the digital SAT harder” question gets answered most honestly, it’s Module 2.


Module 1 is the warmup. It’s a mix of easy, medium, and hard questions designed to sort students into two groups. Module 2 is where the real test begins.


For students routed to the harder Module 2, the difficulty spike is significant. Questions require deeper reasoning, more complex multi-step math, and less predictable passage analysis. The payoff is access to the full 800-point ceiling per section.


For students routed to the easier Module 2, the questions are more straightforward, but the score ceiling clamps down hard at approximately 620-630 per section.


**Strategy implication:** Module 1 accuracy is the single highest priority on test day. Every question you get right in Module 1 helps ensure you’re routed to the harder (and higher-ceiling) Module 2. This is not a test where you can afford a slow start.


Students consistently underestimate how steep the Module 2 difficulty jump can be. The best preparation involves practicing specifically with hard-difficulty questions under timed conditions. A deep[SAT question bank](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/question-bank) that lets you filter by difficulty level is essential for this kind of targeted practice.

## The Verdict: Is the Digital SAT Harder?


Here’s where things stand, honestly and without hedging.


**Compared to the paper SAT:** The digital SAT is not harder by design. College Board’s concordance data confirms that a given score represents the same achievement level regardless of format. But “not harder by design” and “not harder in practice” are two different things. Students who struggle with screen-based reading, who relied on physically marking up passages, or who can’t handle the adaptive pressure may find it genuinely harder. Students who benefit from extra time per question, shorter passages, and Desmos may find it easier.


**Over time:** The digital SAT is getting harder. Module routing thresholds have tightened, specific test dates have been notably more difficult, and practice materials have been recalibrated upward. Students preparing in 2025 and 2026 face a more challenging version than early adopters did.


**In feel:** It’s different. The adaptive mechanism creates psychological pressure the paper test never had. Knowing that your Module 1 performance determines your score ceiling, knowing that the harder Module 2 will challenge you more than anything in Module 1, knowing that Desmos won’t bail you out on the toughest questions: all of this changes the test-taking experience fundamentally.


The students who perform best on the digital SAT are the ones who practice with realistic, adaptive, timed digital simulations. They know what Module 2 feels like before test day. They’ve built Desmos skills and the underlying math knowledge to survive when Desmos can’t help. They’ve trained themselves to read carefully on a screen.


If you want that kind of preparation,[start with a free practice exam](https://miyagilabs.ai/sat/practice-exams) that mirrors the real adaptive format so test day holds no surprises.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is the digital SAT harder than the paper SAT?


Not by College Board’s design. Their concordance studies show that equivalent scores represent the same achievement level. But the adaptive format, screen-based reading, and tighter margins for error make it feel harder for many students, while the shorter length, extra time per question, and Desmos make it feel easier for others. It depends on your strengths and preparation.


### Does the digital SAT get harder as you take it?


Yes, by design. If you perform well on Module 1, you’re routed to a harder Module 2. This is actually a good thing because the harder Module 2 unlocks higher possible scores (up to 800 per section). Students routed to the easier Module 2 are capped at roughly 620-630.


### Is the digital SAT getting harder every year?


The data suggests yes, modestly. Module routing cutoffs have increased, certain 2025 test dates were widely reported as unusually difficult, and College Board’s newer practice tests are harder than the originals. The test is being actively recalibrated.


### What is the hardest part of the digital SAT?


Math Module 2 on the harder path is consistently cited as the most difficult portion. Students and tutors report that it exceeds practice test difficulty and includes questions designed to prevent Desmos-only solving strategies.


### Does everyone get the same digital SAT?


No. While everyone takes the same Module 1, students are routed to different versions of Module 2 based on their Module 1 performance. Additionally, different test dates may use different test forms, though equating adjusts scores to account for difficulty differences.


### Can you still get a good score if you’re routed to the easier Module 2?


You can score up to approximately 620-630 per section on the easier Module 2, even with perfect accuracy. That translates to roughly a 1240-1260 composite ceiling. For many colleges, that’s still a competitive score. For highly selective schools, it likely isn’t enough.


### Is the digital SAT easier than the ACT?


These are fundamentally different tests, and “easier” depends entirely on the student. The digital SAT’s adaptive format rewards strong early performance, while the ACT is linear and time-pressured. Many students benefit from trying both to see which format plays to their strengths. If you’re considering the ACT,[explore ACT prep options](https://miyagilabs.ai/act/prep) to compare.


### How should I prepare differently for the digital SAT?


Practice on a computer or tablet, not paper. Use timed, adaptive practice tests that simulate the real Module 1 to Module 2 routing. Build both Desmos fluency and core math skills. Train yourself to read carefully on a screen. And prioritize Module 1 accuracy above everything else.
